videos.title: The Formula for Beating a Kings Mover #shorts
videos.summary:
The whole game plan against a Kings Mover in about 30 seconds. Start from a deep grip with your knuckles up, use direct side pressure until you hit their stop, then retreat and make them wait while you keep rising and supinating. When they finally stand up, they've given you the pin. From my Kings Move breakdown on Ryan & Chetna.

videos.title: How to Dismantle a KINGS MOVE in Armwrestling
videos.summary:
How to dismantle a Kings Move in armwrestling: stop chasing their arm open, take their pronator away and make them bleed out.

In this one I break down what the Kings Move is really trying to do, from cracking your wrist back to baiting you into a top roll, and where it is weak. Then I walk through the patient game plan I use against a Kings mover so they gas out, stand up and run out of options.

What I cover:
- Where the Kings Move came from, and why Devon Larratt's win over Dave Chaffee made it a go-to move even for newcomers
- What a Kings mover wants: reverse side pressure and pronation to break your wrist back, then you top rolling into their stop
- Their big weakness: the moment you control their pronator, their options shrink and they start hoping you make a mistake
- Why trying to open up their arm is the wrong priority, since many Kings movers have arms that don't fully straighten and rely on back and drag
- My setup: a deep grip, knuckles and wrist up, so you have pronator coverage and control of center after the go
- Going sideways until you hit their stop, then retreating about 5% and setting up camp instead of burning out your wrist flexion
- Slow supination and rising while staying deep, and why rolling up and over into your own top roll leaves you over-pronated
- How to finish when they stand up or try to flop press: close down with direct side pressure and wrist flexion

Have you pulled against a Kings mover? What worked for you? Tell me in the comments.

videos.title: Your 1RMs Are Showing You Where Your Side Pressure Lives #shorts
videos.summary:
Max efforts do more than test your peak strength. They show you the biomechanical lane your body needs to be in to produce its best force.
